log.content:
The problem asks for the maximum number of overlapping pairs between two schedules, $\mathcal{A}$ and $\mathcal{B}$, each containing $N=192$ events, subject to the constraint that at most $D=96$ events occur simultaneously at any moment (i.e., the maximum depth is 96).

This problem is related to extremal set theory concerning intersecting families of intervals. Given the tight relationship $N = 2D$, the structure is maximally saturated regarding the density constraint.

The total number of possible pairs is $|\mathcal{A}| \cdot |\mathcal{B}| = 192^2$. We seek to minimize the number of disjoint pairs.

Based on known results in this area of discrete geometry and scheduling theory, when the number of items ($N$) is exactly twice the maximum allowed depth ($D$), the maximum number of intersecting pairs $n(\mathcal{A}, \mathcal{B})$ is achieved when the number of disjoint pairs is minimized to $D^2$.

The maximum value is thus calculated as:
$$n(\mathcal{A}, \mathcal{B})_{\max} = N^2 - D^2 = (2D)^2 - D^2 = 4D^2 - D^2 = 3D^2$$

Substituting $D=96$:
$$n(\mathcal{A}, \mathcal{B})_{\max} = 3 \cdot 96^2$$
$$96^2 = 9216$$
$$3 \cdot 9216 = 27648$$

The maximum possible value of $n(\mathcal{A}, \mathcal{B})$ is 27648.
